chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdullah said:
Know your Imam, for if you know him, it will not harm you whether this matter (deliverance) comes soon or is delayed.

key_terms.إِمَامَكَ: Your Imam, the divinely appointed leader
key_terms.الْأَمْرِ: The matter/command (referring to deliverance or the Imam's authority)

ai.seo_question: Why is it important to know the Imam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the foundational Shia principle that *ma'rifat al-imam* (recognition of the Imam) is the key to spiritual stability during the period of *al-Ghayba* (Occultation). By firmly knowing the Imam, the believer remains unaffected by the timing of the *al-Amr al-Muntazar* (the awaited affair), whether it is hastened or delayed, thus preserving faith against the confusion of *al-Ghurba* (strangeness).

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (1) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from Ali bin Ibraheem from his father from Hammad bin Eessa from Hurayz from Zurara that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “
Know your imam because if you know him, it does not harm you whether deliverance comes soon or late.”
